newsitem.title: DENMARK: Den Danske doubts 97 core earnings rise.
newsitem.headline: Den Danske doubts 97 core earnings rise.

text.p: Denmark's Den Danske Bank said on Thursday that it saw little prospect for a further rise in core earnings for 1997.
"For 1997 the board states that costs are not expected to fall and it is uncertain if the low level of provisions can be maintained," the bank said in its 1996 annual report.
"An improvement in core earnings can hardly be expected and earnings, therefore, will hardly be sufficent to ensure a completely satisfactory return on own capital," it said.
In its 1996 report the bank, Denmark's biggest, said that core earnings, including the operating result for insurance, rose to 3.730 billion crowns from 2.785 the year before.
But it acknowledged that the bulk of the 945 million crown increase came from a 617 million crown fall in provisions. In addition insurance revenue rose by 407 million crowns.
It said that techological improvement and Nordic expansion precluded cost savings during the coming year.
"Despite tight cost controls, including staff reductions, the bank's costs are not expected to fall," it said.
